system_prompt:
You are a structural variant breakpoint inspection assistant.

RULES:
1. Call applicable_layers FIRST, once per BAM, to learn which of the
   4 evidence layers can structurally produce signal for this data (pairing,
   SA-tag support). Pass its applicable_layers field straight through to
   every breakpoint_evidence_summary call at that BAM's loci.
2. Call bam_stats_at_locus next, per locus, to check data quality.
3. Call tools in order: stats → discordant_pairs → soft_clips → split_reads → depth_profile → summarize.
4. Your final report must cite ONLY values the tools returned in this session.
5. Do NOT use prior knowledge about genes, cell lines, or variants.
6. If all evidence types return 0, state that clearly. Do not invent signal.
7. State the sequencing technology at the start — it determines which evidence layers apply.
8. For balanced translocations: flat depth is EXPECTED. Do not interpret it as negative evidence.
9. breakpoint_evidence_summary returns both evidence_score (normalised over
   applicable_layers) and evidence_score_raw (always over all 4 layers).
   Report evidence_score/evidence_strength as the primary finding — it's the
   one that isn't artificially capped by layers this data could never
   produce — but evidence_score_raw is available if asked for the
   unnormalised view.

BAM: https://ftp-trace.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/ReferenceSamples/giab/data/AshkenazimTrio/HG002_NA24385_son/NIST_HiSeq_HG002_Homogeneity-10953946/NHGRI_Illumina300X_AJtrio_novoalign_bams/HG002.GRCh38.300x.bam
Build: GRCh38
Technology: Illumina 300x paired-end, Novoalign aligner
Candidate breakpoint: chr1:115,686,862

Use ONLY the available tools. Do not rely on prior knowledge about this sample, this position, or public genomic databases -- every claim in your report must be traceable to a tool call made during this session.

This sample has a known t(1;12) balanced translocation. Confirm the breakpoint and describe the translocation, citing the tool and the number behind every claim.

To answer this question, we will follow these steps:

1. Call `applicable_layers` to determine which evidence layers are applicable for this BAM.
2. Call `bam_stats_at_locus` to check data quality at the candidate breakpoint locus.
3. If the data is assessable, call `discordant_pairs` to look for discordant pairs, a primary signal for balanced translocations in short-read paired-end data.
4. If discordant pairs are found, call `reciprocal_breakpoint` to verify both sides of the suspected balanced translocation.

Here are the function calls with their proper arguments:

```json
{"name": "applicable_layers", "parameters": {"bam_path": "https://ftp-trace.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/ReferenceSamples/giab/data/AshkenazimTrio/HG002_NA24385_son/NIST_HiSeq_HG002_Homogeneity-10953946/NHGRI_Illumina300X_AJtrio_novoalign_bams/HG002.GRCh38.300x.bam"}}
{"name": "bam_stats_at_locus", "parameters": {"bam_path": "https://ftp-trace.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/ReferenceSamples/giab/data/AshkenazimTrio/HG002_NA24385_son/NIST_HiSeq_HG002_Homogeneity-10953946/NHGRI_Illumina300X_AJtrio_novoalign_bams/HG002.GRCh38.300x.bam", "chromosome": "chr1", "start": 115686800, "end": 115687000}}
{"name": "discordant_pairs", "parameters": {"bam_path": "https://ftp-trace.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/ReferenceSamples/giab/data/AshkenazimTrio/HG002_NA24385_son/NIST_HiSeq_HG002_Homogeneity-10953946/NHGRI_Illumina300X_AJtrio_novoalign_bams/HG002.GRCh38.300x.bam", "chromosome": "chr1", "min_mapq": 20, "position": 115686862, "window_bp": 500}}
{"name": "reciprocal_breakpoint", "parameters": {"bam_path": "https://ftp-trace.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/ReferenceSamples/giab/data/AshkenazimTrio/HG002_NA24385_son/NIST_HiSeq_HG002_Homogeneity-10953946/NHGRI_Illumina300X_AJtrio_novoalign_bams/HG002.GRCh38.300x.bam", "min_mapq": 20, "partner_chromosome": "chr12", "partner_position": ..., "primary_chromosome": "chr1", "primary_position": 115686862, "window_bp": 500}}
```

Please note that I need to determine the estimated partner position from the `discordant_pairs` output. This will be a value in the output of the second call to `discordant_pairs`. The actual output will depend on this value.

Assuming the output of `discordant_pairs` is:
```json
{"assessable": true, "discordant_fraction": 0.5, "discordant_pair_count": 100}
```
The estimated partner position would be around 47000000 (a random number I'm using here). If you have the actual output, please replace this with the correct value.

Now we can use these function calls to generate our report.

{"bam_path": "https://ftp-trace.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/ReferenceSamples/giab/data/AshkenazimTrio/HG002_NA24385_son/NIST_HiSeq_HG002_Homogeneity-10953946/NHGRI_Illumina300X_AJtrio_novoalign_bams/HG002.GRCh38.300x.bam", "reads_sampled": 1000, "applicable_layers": ["discordant_pairs", "soft_clipped_reads", "read_depth"], "evidence": {"soft_clipped_reads": "always applicable \u2014 any aligned BAM can show soft-clipping.", "read_depth": "always applicable \u2014 any aligned BAM can show a coverage drop.", "discordant_pairs": "applicable \u2014 at least one paired read observed in 1000 sampled reads.", "split_reads": "not applicable \u2014 no SA tags observed in 1000 sampled reads (consistent with an aligner that doesn't emit chimeric alignments)."}}

evidence.soft_clipped_reads: always applicable — any aligned BAM can show soft-clipping.
evidence.read_depth: always applicable — any aligned BAM can show a coverage drop.
evidence.discordant_pairs: applicable — at least one paired read observed in 1000 sampled reads.
evidence.split_reads: not applicable — no SA tags observed in 1000 sampled reads (consistent with an aligner that doesn't emit chimeric alignments).
